key_insight: Imperfect physics improves regression convergence rates only below a modeling-error threshold; with exact physics, studied PDE classes yield rates corresponding to dimension d−1 rather than d.
engineering_relevance: The results clarify when PDE constraints can improve statistical efficiency and give conditions for near-linear estimator computation and tuning without knowing the modeling error.
method: Benchmark physics-informed regression against optimal smoothness-only regression.
Derive a modeling-error threshold for all linear PDEs and certain nonlinear PDEs.
Prove minimax-optimal rates up to logarithmic factors for classes of constant-coefficient elliptic and hyperbolic PDEs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence-rate and minimax guarantees, but no empirical datasets or experimental benchmarks.
watch_item: Rate gains depend on PDE type and modeling error, while near-linear computation requires additional conditions.
paper_title: Minimax Rates for imperfect Physics-Informed Regression
